name: corpus-reproduction
title: BioModels corpus reproduction — every model across every simulator

at_a_glance.role: The full corpus sweep — every BioModel across every available simulator — establishing corpus-scale COVERAGE, surfaced through the corpus explorer.
The agreement check — live engines vs the BioSimulators SED-ML reference on the BIOMD1-3 validation subset — showing residuals are observable coverage, not numerical divergence.

biological_story: BioModels is the community's curated library of published quantitative biology models. Reproducing it across independent simulators is the basic reproducibility test for the standards (SBML/SED-ML) the field relies on.
question: Across the full BioModels corpus, do independent ODE simulators (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) reproduce the same trajectories for the same model — and where do they diverge?
hypothesis: Standards-based SBML/SED-ML models should integrate to the same solution regardless of engine; systematic cross-engine disagreement flags either a model-encoding ambiguity or an engine-specific numerical behaviour, not a "correct" answer.

executive.what_is_this: A corpus-scale reproduction study: every BioModel we could fetch and parse (1008 models) was simulated under up to five independent ODE engines (amici, copasi, pysces, simbio, tellurium) via the batch-compare-biomodels composite, fanned out over the whole corpus with the Ray runner. The full per-model, per-engine, per-variable timecourse (14.7M rows) is the result; the corpus explorer (Analyses tab) browses it model-by-model.
executive.verdict: Reproduced at corpus scale, with agreement validated on a subset. COVERAGE: 1008 models ran; 306 have all five engines and 725 have four or more — a broad, engine-independent cross-run of the BioModels corpus (full-corpus study). AGREEMENT: on the BIOMD1-3 validation subset, every live engine reproduces the BioSimulators reference exactly wherever an observable is computed, and the residual failures are observable-coverage, not numerical divergence (repeat-matching study). Corpus-wide scored agreement is not yet quantified; per-model agreement is inspectable in the corpus explorer.

scientific_argument.main_claim: A standards-based multi-simulator reproduction of the BioModels corpus is feasible and repeatable. Coverage is demonstrated corpus-wide (1008 models, up to five engines); exact cross-engine/reference agreement is demonstrated on a validation subset, where the only residual is missing SED-ML observables, not divergent trajectories. The corpus-wide agreement claim is therefore scoped: supported by the subset result plus per-model explorability, pending a corpus-wide scored run.
evidence_for: 1008 models simulated across up to five engines (14.7M timecourse rows); committed as a single tidy parquet with a compact per-model index.
306 models cover all five engines and 725 cover four or more — a genuine cross-engine reproduction, not a two-engine spot check.

On BIOMD1-3, all 12 repeat arms match the BioSimulators reference exactly (numpy allclose) where observables are computed; residuals are coverage (iter1 17/48 missing → iter2 0 on BIOMD1-2, 2 on BIOMD3), not numerics.
The corpus explorer overlays every engine per variable for any model, so agreement and divergence are directly visible.

studies.name: full-corpus-reproduction
studies.title: Full BioModels reproduction across all simulators (1008 models × 5 engines)
studies.question: Across the entire BioModels corpus, do independent simulators (COPASI, Tellurium, simbio, AMICI, PySCeS) reproduce the same trajectories, and where do they diverge?

findings.statement: Corpus-scale reproduction is feasible and repeatable: 1008 BioModels were fetched, parsed and simulated under up to five independent ODE engines (14.7M timecourse rows), committed as one tidy parquet + per-model index.

Coverage is broad, not a two-engine spot check: 306 models carry all five engines and 725 carry four or more. Per-engine reach is uneven — tellurium 985, amici 879, copasi 870, pysces 770, simbio 367 — so simbio is the coverage-limiting engine, not a correctness-limiting one.
findings.next_action: Investigate why simbio covers fewer models (parse/feature gaps) to raise five-engine coverage above 306.

findings.statement: This study measures COVERAGE, not scored trajectory agreement. Whether the overlapping engines actually agree per-model is inspectable in the corpus explorer and quantified on the BIOMD1-3 subset by the repeat-matching study (exact agreement where observables are computed). The corpus-wide agreement claim is therefore scoped — supported by the subset result plus per-model explorability, not yet a corpus-wide scored number.
findings.next_action: Run the repeat-/reproducibility-match scorer across the full corpus against the BioSimulators reference to replace explorability with a corpus-wide agreement statistic.

studies.claim: Running the full BioModels corpus through the batch-compare-biomodels composite under up to five independent ODE engines reproduces 1008 models (14.7M timecourse rows) at corpus scale: 306 models are covered by all five engines and 725 by four or more. This study establishes COVERAGE — how broadly each model is cross-run and that the per-model, per-engine trajectories are committed and browsable model-by-model in the corpus explorer. Scored trajectory AGREEMENT against the BioSimulators reference is measured in the sibling repeat-matching study (currently on the BIOMD1-3 validation subset), not quantified corpus-wide here.

biological_validation.basis: Both coverage gates pass (n_models >= 1000; n_models_ge_4_engines >= 700). These certify corpus-scale coverage; scored agreement is the sibling study's gate, not this one's.

regression_compatibility.basis: The Ray fan-out completed corpus-wide (crash-isolated per model); the committed parquet + index are the reproducible artifact.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-03 draws the line between coverage (established here) and scored agreement (repeat-matching), preventing the common overclaim that broad coverage equals demonstrated cross-engine agreement.

derived.insight: Corpus-scale reproduction is feasible and repeatable: 1008 BioModels were fetched, parsed and simulated under up to five independent ODE engines (14.7M timecourse rows), committed as one tidy parquet + per-model index.

studies.name: repeat-matching
studies.title: Repeat- and reproducibility-matching vs the BioSimulators reference study
studies.question: Do the current cross-simulator BioModels runs reproduce the BioSimulators SED-ML reference results engine-for-engine (repeat matching), and where they diverge, can any previous cross-engine open questions be closed (reproducibility matching)?

findings.statement: After the iteration-2 coverage fix, every repeat arm reproduces the BioSimulators reference exactly: 12/12 arms have matched == total under numpy allclose, with zero numerical mismatches.
findings.next_action: Scale the repeat-match harness to the full corpus against the complete BioSimulators reference set.

findings.statement: The residual failures are coverage, not numerics: iteration 1 left 17/48 reference observables uncomputed on BIOMD1-2; iteration 2 closed that to 0 there and 2 on BIOMD3 (SED-ML dataGenerator forms not yet supported). This confirms the hypothesis that the dominant failure mode is missing observables rather than divergent trajectories.
findings.next_action: Implement the remaining SED-ML dataGenerator shapes to close the BIOMD3 2-observable gap.

findings.statement: Cross-engine reproducibility is exact where observables overlap: 22/30 iter2 pairs match fully. The 8 residuals are understood — pysces computes 2/65 observables differently from copasi/tellurium/amici on BIOMD1, and simbio exposes a reduced 48-observable set (those 48 all agree). simbio, the new engine, lands on the engines that already agree.
findings.next_action: Investigate the 2 pysces observables on BIOMD1 and simbio's reduced observable export.

studies.claim: On the BIOMD1-3 validation subset, the live engines reproduce the BioSimulators SED-ML reference arm exactly wherever an observable is computed: after iteration 2 ("full observable coverage"), all 12 repeat arms (copasi/tellurium/amici/pysces × the models they cover) match the reference under numpy allclose with zero numerical mismatches; the only residual is coverage (2 reference observables in BIOMD3 are not yet computed by any engine). Cross-engine reproducibility is likewise exact where observables overlap (22/30 pairs exact; the 8 residuals are pysces computing 2/65 observables differently and simbio exposing a reduced 48-observable set). The dominant failure mode is observable coverage, not numerical divergence — confirming the study hypothesis.

biological_validation.basis: On the 3-model validation subset the repeat-match gate passes: all computed observables reproduce the BioSimulators reference exactly. Scope is the subset, not the full corpus.

regression_compatibility.basis: Both iterations completed without error; the iter2 run is committed and re-scoreable from the parquet.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-02 identifies the mechanism — residual mismatch is observable coverage (unsupported SED-ML dataGenerators), not numerical divergence — which redirects effort from "chase trajectory differences" to "finish dataGenerator support".

derived.insight: After the iteration-2 coverage fix, every repeat arm reproduces the BioSimulators reference exactly: 12/12 arms have matched == total under numpy allclose, with zero numerical mismatches.
